newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases with good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases with good liquidity.

text.p: German call money rates eased slightly to around 3.03/3.07 percent from 3.05/3.07 percent with an increase in reserve holdings allaying fears of tight money conditions this month.
German traders flately rejected speculation in London that the Bundesbank may adopt a variable rate securities repurcahse agreement at its meeting on Thursday.

The said the speculation was born of the fact that the Bundesbank will hold a press conference following its council meeting, maybe missunderstanding that the press conference is a regular summer event.
The Bundesbank later said it would keep the repo rate steady at a fixed 3.00 percent and also left interest rates unchanged.
Money traders said an increase in the amount credit institutions held with the Bundesbank showed the money market has sufficient liquidity.
Credit institutions held 42 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Wednesday, up from 40.9 billin marks on Tuesday.
No appreciable amount of funds were borrowed from the Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.07483 percent on Thursday compared with 3.08692 percent on Wednesday.
